fullPassage:
When we ask ourselves what makes us happy, we often think of the circumstances we are in, what we have, or whom we are with. From a biological point of view, however, happiness is largely a chemical experience. Four main brain chemicals are responsible for creating the sensations and emotions we associate with happiness: endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, and oxytocin.
It is good news for us that happiness can be controlled. Even when our lives aren't exactly what we would like them to be, we can improve our mood by engaging in pleasant and healthy activities that increase the amounts of these happiness chemicals. Let's take a deeper dive into what each of these chemicals does and how we can increase their levels.
Endorphins are natural pain relievers. They are "feel-good" chemicals because they can make you feel better and put you in a positive state of mind. When our body feels pain or stress, the brain releases endorphins to block the nerve cells that receive the pain signals. This essentially turns off your pain, helping you continue functioning, even in painful and stressful situations.
The most well-known way to increase endorphins is through slightly challenging exercise which makes you a little short of breath. Research shows that about twenty to thirty minutes of exercise can help boost your endorphin levels significantly. Another way is to have a good laugh. Share funny videos, tell jokes, and laugh with your friends. We don't laugh because we are happy; we are happy because we laugh.
Serotonin is another brain chemical that plays a key role in balancing our mood. It provides feelings of happiness and also helps decrease our worries and concerns. When you feel happy and all seems right with the world, you are feeling the effects of serotonin.
Serotonin is made from the essential amino acid tryptophan, which must enter our body through our diet. Therefore, eating foods rich in tryptophan like chicken, beans, eggs, and nuts can boost your body's natural ability to make serotonin. Furthermore, good habits like getting more sunshine and going on short walks can do wonders for boosting your levels of serotonin.
Dopamine is an important chemical for motivation. It is called the "reward chemical" because it rewards the brain with happy feelings for meeting goals and achieving things. We can also feel a dopamine rush when we imagine a future achievement. In both cases, dopamine gives us feelings of joy and satisfaction, encouraging us to seek out more goals and find new challenges.
Choosing food higher in protein can be a good way to increase your dopamine levels naturally, because it can only be made with the amino acid tyrosine, which is found in many proteins. Getting regular, high-quality sleep may also help keep your dopamine levels balanced and help you feel more alert during the day. Meditation has also been shown to increase dopamine levels. This, in turn, leads to improved focus and concentration.
Oxytocin is often called the "love hormone" because it promotes social bonding and trust. It is mainly associated with loving touches and close relationships. Oxytocin will be released when you are connecting with people, and it reduces your stress level and calms down your nervous system.
Spending time with friends and loved ones is a great way to raise your oxytocin levels. Giving or receiving a massage, shaking hands, or hugging can lead to higher levels of oxytocin as well. If you have a pet, you can increase oxytocin for both yourself and your pet by hugging your little friend.
You may have heard the saying "Happiness depends on your attitude, not on what you have." Endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, and oxytocin help promote happiness, and you can give these happiness chemicals a natural boost with simple activities. We cannot always choose the situations we find ourselves in, but we can certainly choose what to do for ourselves. There's a lot we can do to boost the happiness chemicals in our brains. This means that we have control of our own happiness!

questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 엔도르핀 작용 순서: 통증/스트레스 → 엔도르핀 방출(B) → 신경세포 차단(C) → 통증 차단 결과(A).
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C)
❌ ② (B)-(A)-(C)
✅ ③ (B)-(C)-(A)
❌ ④ (C)-(A)-(B)
✅ (B)-(C)-(A): 원인(통증) → 방출 → 차단 → 결과의 논리적 순서. ❌ 나머지: 인과관계 흐름 깨짐.
det.tip: 순서배열: 원인→과정→결과 순서. 지시어/연결어 단서: 'This'는 앞 내용 가리킴.

questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 세로토닌: 역할(B) → 원료 설명(C) → Therefore 결론(A).
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C)
❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B)
❌ ③ (C)-(A)-(B)
✅ ④ (B)-(C)-(A)
✅ (B)-(C)-(A): 역할 → 원료 → 따라서 음식 권장. 'Therefore'가 (C) 뒤에 와야 함. ❌ 나머지: Therefore의 위치가 어색.
det.tip: Therefore(따라서): 앞 내용의 결론. (C)의 트립토판 설명 → (A)의 음식 권장.

questions.stem:
다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"It rewards not only past accomplishments but also future possibilities."

det.korean: '과거 성취뿐 아니라 미래의 가능성에도 보상한다'는 과거 성취(②) + 미래 상상(③) 모두 설명한 뒤에 요약하는 위치.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: ② 뒤에 미래 성취 상상 언급, ③ 뒤의 'In both cases'가 이 문장과 자연 연결. ❌ ①: 아직 보상 설명 전. ❌ ②: 미래 가능성 언급 전. ❌ ④: 이미 요약 완료.
det.tip: 'In both cases'가 삽입 문장의 두 가지(past + future)를 받아줌.

questions.stem:
다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"In other words, physical contact and emotional closeness are key triggers for this chemical."

det.korean: '즉, 신체 접촉과 정서적 친밀감이 핵심 촉발 요인'은 'loving touches and close relationships' 직후에 부연.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: ① 뒤의 'loving touches and close relationships'를 'In other words'로 부연. ❌ ①: 아직 접촉 언급 전. ❌ ③④: 구체적 방법 나열 중간.
det.tip: 'In other words(즉)'은 앞 문장을 다른 표현으로 다시 설명.

questions.passage: The most well-known way to increase endorphins is through slightly ①<u>challenging</u> exercise which makes you a little short of breath. Research shows that about twenty to thirty minutes of exercise can help ②<u>boosting</u> your endorphin levels significantly. Another way is to have a good laugh. Share funny videos, tell jokes, and ③<u>laugh</u> with your friends. We don't laugh because we are happy; we ④<u>are</u> happy because we laugh.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 운동이 엔도르핀 수치를 높이는 데 도움이 된다. help + 동사원형/to V.
det.analysis: ✅ ①challenging: 현재분사 형용사. ❌ ②boosting: help + boost(원형) 또는 help + to boost. boosting은 틀림. ✅ ③laugh: 명령문 동사원형. ✅ ④are: we are happy 정상.
det.tip: help (to) V: help boosting (X) → help boost / help to boost (O).

questions.passage: Oxytocin is often called the "love hormone" because it ①<u>promotes</u> social bonding and trust. It is mainly ②<u>associated</u> with loving touches and close relationships. Oxytocin will be released when you are connecting with people, and it ③<u>reduce</u> your stress level. Spending time with friends and ④<u>loved</u> ones is a great way to raise your oxytocin levels.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 옥시토신이 스트레스 수준을 줄인다. 주어 it(3인칭 단수).
det.analysis: ✅ ①promotes: it(단수) 일치. ✅ ②associated: be associated with 정상. ❌ ③reduce: 주어 it → reduces 필요. ✅ ④loved: 과거분사 형용사 'loved ones'.
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어 + 동사-s: it reduces (O) / it reduce (X).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 각 화학물질이 무엇을 하는지. each는 단수 → does.
det.analysis: ✅ ①what: 관계대명사 what(~하는 것). ✅ ②that: 관계대명사, activities 수식. ❌ ③do: each(단수) → does 필요. ✅ ④how: 간접의문문 접속사.
det.tip: each + 단수동사: each does (O) / each do (X).

questions.passage: The most well-known way to increase endorphins is through slightly challenging exercise which makes you a little short of breath. Research shows that about twenty to thirty minutes of exercise can help boost your endorphin levels ①<u>significantly</u>. Another way is to have a good laugh. Share funny videos, tell jokes, and laugh with your friends. We don't laugh because we are ②<u>happy</u>; we are happy because we ③<u>laugh</u>. Serotonin is another brain chemical that plays a key role in ④<u>disrupting</u> our mood.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 세로토닌은 기분 균형(balancing)에 역할을 한다. disrupting(방해하는)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①significantly: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②happy: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③laugh: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④disrupting: 원문은 balancing. 기분을 '균형잡는' 것이지 '방해하는' 것이 아님.
det.tip: balancing(균형잡는) ↔ disrupting(방해하는, 혼란시키는).

questions.passage: Choosing food higher in protein can be a good way to increase your dopamine levels ①<u>naturally</u>, because it can only be made with the amino acid tyrosine. Meditation has also been shown to increase dopamine levels. This, in turn, leads to improved focus and ④<u>concentration</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수면이 낮에 더 기민하게(alert) 느끼게 해준다. drowsy(졸린)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①naturally: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②balanced: 원문 그대로. ❌ ③drowsy: 원문은 alert(기민한). 졸린 것이 아니라 깨어있는 것. ✅ ④concentration: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: alert(기민한, 깨어있는) ↔ drowsy(졸린, 나른한). 수면이 낮의 활력을 높인다는 맥락.

ch: Eating foods rich in protein is the best method
Physical contact like hugging or shaking hands can also help

det.korean: 옥시토신 증가 방법: 친구와 시간 보내기 + 포옹이나 악수 같은 신체 접촉.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 원문 'hugging, shaking hands'와 일치. ❌ ②: 단백질은 도파민. ❌ ③: 운동은 엔도르핀. ❌ ④: 명상/수면은 도파민.
det.tip: 옥시토신 = 사회적 유대 + 신체 접촉. 각 화학물질별 증가 방법 구분.

questions.stem: 위 글의 도파민에 대한 설명과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'simple activities' + 'control of our own happiness'. ❌ ①: 발견 과정이 아닌 활용법. ❌ ③: 부작용 언급 없음. ❌ ④: 환경 변화가 아닌 활동으로 통제.
det.tip: 글 결론부의 핵심 메시지: we have control of our own happiness.

questions.passage: Dopamine is an important chemical for motivation. It is called the "reward chemical" because it rewards the brain with happy feelings for meeting goals and achieving things. We can also feel a dopamine rush when we imagine a future achievement. In both cases, dopamine gives us feelings of joy and satisfaction, encouraging us to seek out more goals and find new challenges. Choosing food higher in protein can be a good way to increase your dopamine levels naturally, because <u>it</u> can only be made with the amino acid tyrosine.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'it'이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 도파민은 아미노산 타이로신으로만 만들어진다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①dopamine: 'increase your dopamine levels... because it can only be made with...' → it = dopamine. ❌ ②protein: 단백질은 만들어지는 대상 아님. ❌ ③food: 음식도 아님. ❌ ④motivation: 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: it = 문장의 주제 dopamine. '타이로신으로만 만들어질 수 있다'의 주어.

questions.passage: When we ask ourselves what makes us happy, we often think of the circumstances we are in, what we have, or whom we are with. From a biological point of view, however, happiness is largely a chemical experience. Four main brain chemicals are responsible for creating the sensations and emotions we associate with happiness: endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, and oxytocin. It is good news for us that happiness can be controlled. Even when our lives aren't exactly what we would like them to be, we can improve our mood by engaging in pleasant and healthy activities that increase the amounts of these happiness chemicals. Let's take a deeper dive into what each of these chemicals does and how we can increase their levels. Endorphins are natural pain relievers. They are "feel-good" chemicals because they can make you feel better and put you in a positive state of mind.
questions.stem: 본문에서 찾아 다음 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오. "행복과 관련된 감각과 감정을 만드는 네 가지 뇌 화학물질은 endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, 그리고 __________이다.". (1단어)

det.korean: 네 가지: endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, oxytocin.
det.analysis: ✅ oxytocin: 원문에서 직접 찾을 수 있는 네 번째 화학물질.
det.tip: 네 가지 행복 화학물질: endorphins, serotonin, dopamine, oxytocin.

det.analysis: ✅ satisfaction: sense of + 명사. satisfy(동사) → satisfaction(명사).
det.tip: satisfy(만족시키다, 동사) → satisfaction(만족, 명사). a sense of satisfaction = 만족감.

det.analysis: ✅ into(전치사) + what each of these chemicals does(간접의문문) + and(접속사) + how we can increase their levels(간접의문문).
det.tip: take a deeper dive into: ~을 더 깊이 탐구하다. 간접의문문: 의문사 + 주어 + 동사.
